en: O, let me see — lift your eyes and look:
why this haze of sleep in your eyes?
I have drunk, it seems, of something —
some wine brimming with nectar.
That is why there is a haze of sleep in my eyes.
Fie, fie, fie!
Friend, what is the harm?
(In this world) some are so wise, some absent-minded,
some are aware, some unaware,
in someone's eyes a gleam of laughter,
in someone's eyes, tears.
In my eyes only a haze of sleep.
Friend, why so nearly motionless,
here, standing in the tree's shade?
Numb under the heart's burden, these feet
do not wish to move,
so I stand in the tree's shade.
Fie, fie, fie!
Friend, what is the harm?
(In this world) some lie fallen, some walk away,
some in languor do not wish to move,
some are free in themselves, while someone's
feet are caught in a snare.
Someone's eyes are touched with a daze.
There is no understanding him — come away, come away.
What words he speaks, friend, and with what eyes he gazes!
Come away, come away.
Shame breaks, and in the end I die of shame,
in vain pursuit —
he will not be caught; say, who can hold him?
He himself knows where his heart is.
Come away, come away.
Day and night, as though for someone
I wait in hope upon hope.
(So) my heart is startled, my ears alert,
my eyes thirsty and restless.
Grown restless, I wander round and round,
always thinking — what if I catch sight of her!
"Who comes?" I start and look up
when a bird calls in the grove.
Awake, I cannot see her,
so I wait in hope of dreams —
if behind the veil of sleep she yields herself,
I will bind her in a snare of dream.
The one I love so much, the one I want so much —
it never feels that she is not near,
as if this longing, with its desperate surge,
will call her and bring her here.
Friend, whatever you give of your own free wish, I will take.
Ah me, ah me, beggar of longing,
in your heart of hearts you want my heart and soul.
If you give a flower, I will lift it to my head;
if a thorn is given,
that too I will bear.
Ah me, ah me, beggar of longing,
in your heart of hearts you want my heart and soul.
If once you gaze, friend, with sweet eyes,
drinking the nectar of those eyes
I will stay drunk with it all my life.
If all I meet is a hard sidelong glance,
that too I will carry all my life, driven into my heart.
Ah me, ah me, beggar of longing,
in your heart of hearts you want my heart and soul.
I am desperate to speak my heart's word,
yet no one asked.
He never came, the one to whom I offered
this life, this heart, this body.
Does he watch the road for me,
does he sing the song of parting —
he whose flute-note I heard
when I forsook my home?
For a moment's span shyness held me back,
and the heart's word went unspoken.
For a whole lifetime, for that alone,
the heart's ache has remained.
O friend, let me see, let me see where your heart is.
How the anguished heart wanders round and round — see whom it begs for.
What honey, what nectar, what fragrance,
what beauty you have kept hidden!
On what morning, in what sun's light,
will you open it, and to whom?
What if he never comes in this life,
never finds the path to this grove!
And those who came — when spring is spent,
what if they turn back after all with despairing hearts!
This is no game, no game.
This is the burning anguish of the heart, friend.
This is a restlessness that fills the soul,
the hidden ache of the inmost heart,
this is life and death poured out toward someone's feet.
Someone, it seems, forever
calls me and leaves me desperate;
my soul strains to go, and I cannot go.
The word I long to speak —
that word, it seems, cannot be spoken;
where shall I set down, friend, this basket of love?
Strung with such care, yet in the end I cannot place the garland.
Who that one is, friend, is plain now,
the one to whom our friend has offered heart and soul.
Oh who is he — who, who?
There beneath the tree, a graceful garland at his throat,
who knows on what pretext he sits and stays.
Friend, what will come of it?
Will he ever come near, will he ever speak?
Does he know love, does he own any bond?
By what charm of maya has he taken the heart?
Raising entranced eyes, he gazes into eyes,
as if he lost his way and came here, who knows where. (Oh)
As if some strain of song fills his ears,
as if he is drowned in the light of some moon.
That sweet face rises in my mind.
I will not forget it in this life,
whether in dream or in waking.
Whether you know it or know it not,
in my mind a sweet flute seems always to play,
because you are always here in my heart.
I cannot give it voice,
I only gaze with anguished eyes.
How will you catch him, friend, if you have given yourself away?
How will you make him weep, if you weep yourself?
If you would win a heart, keep your heart hidden.
Who will bind him, when you have bound yourself?
Come near, and no one stays near.
Speak, and no one speaks back.
Once they have you in hand, they drop you to the ground and go.
Beseech them weeping, and they turn their face away smiling.
The one I have loved with all my heart —
can he turn me away, friend?
I stay outside the world;
I do not know what goes on in the world.
Who knows — here, when a soul wants someone with all its life,
whether it wins him or not (I do not know) —
so I have come in fear and trembling,
to an unknown heart's door.
I love everything that is yours —
that wealth of beauty,
that play, that song, that honeyed smile.
With all this you have covered my life over —
where is your limit within this world?
Who are you, and why declare your longing to my friend?
Who cares to know whether you love or love not?
The moon laughs, the evening laughs, the bower-garden is in bloom,
youth laughs, opening in the heart's springtime.
Why do you heave sighs — why do you not laugh?
Have you come to break up the game,
this festival of hearts between friend and friend?
Take your own grief, your own shadow, and go.
Step aside from life's road of joy.
Worship from afar the one enthroned on the heart's lotus.
Then be happy, be happy — I go — I go.
Friend, call him back — no use in this idle game.
Do not be impatient, friend —
no one returns when hope is sated;
keep hope waiting, and they return.
I was alone in that world of my own —
where is this that I have come to?
I do not know the paths here — let me go back.
If only I might find again that house of rest.
Friend, call him back.
No use in idle play, in idle slights.
Do not be impatient, friend —
no one returns when hope is sated;
keep hope waiting, and they return.
Where has it gone, that abode of peace, that world?
That sun, moon, and stars, that grief-stilling evening breeze,
that beauty, that shade, that dream.
Where has it gone, that rest of my own within my own heart?
In whom shall the homeless heart take refuge?
(To Shanta) I have come back; I have known you;
I have brought my heart to your feet —
grant me the cool nectar of your tenderness,
give love, give peace, give new life.
You were near, you went far — now from afar come near.
You roamed the world; she is sitting there still.
There was no light of love; you could not know her well.
Now in the fire of parting the fire of love is ablaze!
Take care, friend — do not love me by mistake.
Do not come near because I love you.
Do whatever makes you happy, friend;
do not smile only so that I may be happy.
I am well enough with my own parting-sorrow;
what good, in endless dark, is a moment's light?
I let go of hope and drift — what will be, will be;
do not drift into the current of my fate.
I had made an error, and the error has broken.
This time I have woken, I have come to know;
this time no more error, no more error.
I have trailed along behind maya,
I have learned that dreams are all false.
The thorn of desire has pierced my soul —
this is no flower, no flower!
If I find love, I will not treat it with scorn,
I will not play games with a heart.
In that love-filled soul I will take shelter, friend —
this world is a fathomless sea,
and this is no shore, no shore!
The bee goes back again and again,
the bee comes back again and again.
Only then does the flower unfold.
The bud longs to open and opens not — dying of shyness, dying of dread.
Forget pride and slight, give heart and soul, stay near night and day.
Oh, give up hope, and still keep hope alive,
in hope of the heart's jewel.
Come back, come back — the wood is drunk with the scent of flowers.
Tonight, on this night of parting, the full-blown blossom floats in dew-water.
Who is that, calling me back?
Who remembers the one who has come back?
Whose heart aches because I went away?
Whose heart's word stays shut within the heart?
I understand only, friend, plain speech —
a plain heart, and plain love.
You all have so much — so many minds and hearts;
do not cast my heart into peril.
The one you sent away with tears in your eyes —
by what pretext will you bring him back now?
Tonight, in the honeyed breeze, at midnight in the flower-grove,
has he risen in your mind beneath the bakul tree?
By what pretext now will you bring him back?
That day too the honeyed night had melted into the soul,
all ten directions budding with petals of flowers.
If two words of tenderness had passed in whispers,
if you had slipped that garland around his neck —
by what pretext will you bring him back now?
The honeyed night of the full moon comes back again and again;
the one who has gone away comes back no more.
The hour was in our favor — only a moment's error,
and forever the thirst-stricken heart burns.
by what pretext will you bring him back now?
Whom have you, unknowing, set adrift in tears?
Oh, who is left gazing down the empty road?
Whose life is without joy, whose soul burns?
You never read the language of someone's eyes,
never grasped the hope of someone's heart,
never turned to see
whose desperate heart's longing you have come trampling down.
I understand no one else — you alone I have understood.
In you I have found light in the dark of doubt.
I have roamed this world and won no one's heart;
only into your heart have I entered.
In this world who will turn me away, who will call and take me in?
Even now I cannot tell — I live on in fear.
You alone I know; your word I have understood;
in you I have found shore upon a shoreless sea.
Night has passed into dawn, roaming the grove;
the parting-stricken heart has died of weeping.
The pale moon has set, the pale smile has faded,
and the heart broke out weeping in an anguished strain.
Come, friend, come then — let us turn back home;
let the pale eyes drift away in their own tears.
Let the empty heart break; let hope come to its end;
let the one the heart calls stay far away.
Come, come, Spring, to the earth.
Bring the cuckoo's call, songs of love,
bring the languid breeze laden with the wine of fragrance;
bring the swell of new youth, new life,
fresh blossoming desire to the earth.
Come trembling and shivering, murmurous with rustling,
thrilled with new leaves,
in the bower of malati vines restless with flowers,
in happy shade, on honeyed airs — come, come.
Come to the lap of young dawn, her lotus feet flushed with sunrise.
Come in the midnight swooning with moonlight,
on the bank of the rippling, murmuring river,
in lake waters happily asleep — come, come.
Come into hearts aching with youth,
come into eyes languid with the joy of union,
come into the midst of sweet shyness,
bind arm to arm,
and with new blossoms weave a new bond of union.
